affected_predicate.description: A saved, non-all-day calendar event titled 'Board Meeting' matches Carl's November 15 meeting at 3 PM and lasts one hour.

competing_trace_defects.description: Step 10 clicked an already-off All-day toggle while claiming to turn it off, visibly changing it to on and temporarily preventing entry of specific start and end times.

chains.rationale: At the reuse target, the repeated toggle action changed All-day from on to off, visibly correcting the independently introduced step-10 state rather than producing a continuing defect. Subsequent actions set the start to 2 PM and end to 3 PM, save the event, and open a visible October 16 entry titled 'Board Meeting' showing 02:00 PM–03:00 PM. Thus the harmful toggle state was recovered at step 11 and did not remain continuous. The target is classified as merely concurrent with failure-oriented attribution because its observed effect is corrective, not harmful.

summary: The sole strict-MHR reuse target repeats a false toggle instruction but visibly restores the event from all-day to timed mode. The trace then shows a saved one-hour 'Board Meeting' event from 2 PM to 3 PM, so the reused action does not exhibit a continuing harmful mechanism.
